• Nearly the entire population, including over one million children, is estimated to require
protection services and mental health and psychosocial support (Flash Appeal, December
2025 and UNICEF, December 2025).
• >58,000 children have lost one or both parents (source: UNICEF, December 2025).
• >918,000 people are estimated to be living in close proximity to identiﬁed explosive
ordnance threats (source: Protection Cluster, as of September 2026).

WATER SANITATION AND HYGIENE

*

• 91% of assessed households faced moderate to high levels of water insecurity in the 30
days prior to early August.
• 31% of assessed households had total water access below minimum humanitarian
standards (15L/person/day), including 57% below minimum for drinking water
(6L/person/day).
• 88% of assessed households reported facing challenges in accessing safe and clean
sanitation facilities.
• 92% of key informants reported that householders are facing barriers to accessing
hygiene and non-food items, primarily due to insuﬃcient distributions and high cost of
items when available on the market.
• 39% of assessed households reported solid waste accumulation in their vicinity, and
36% observed sewage/sludge near their shelters.
• 69% of assessed households reported cases of skin diseases in the 30 days prior to early August.
• 81% of assessed households reported availability of soap at their shelters.

*Source: WASH Cluster telephone-based Light-Touch Monitoring 5-12 August 2026. Findings are not statistically
representative of the population.

NUTRITION*

• >2,900 children aged 6-59 months were admitted for malnutrition treatment in August
including over 390 with Severe Acute Malnutrition (source: Nutrition Cluster).
• 30% of infants and young children under two years achieve minimum dietary diversity.
• 7.2% of pregnant and breastfeeding women found to be acutely malnourished.
• 12.2% of infants and young children under ﬁve affected by stunting, indicating prolonged
nutritional deprivation.
• ~74,200 children aged 6-59 months and ~24,600 pregnant and breastfeeding women
are expected to require nutrition treatment or support between May 2026 and April 2027.
These include >11,400 severe cases among children (source: IPC, 23 July 2026).
*Source: Nutrition Cluster SMART survey as of July 2026, unless otherwise noted.
**These figures reflect recent updates from partners.

EDUCATION*

• ~771,200 pre-school (114,000) and school-aged (~657,200) children in Gaza require education
support for the 2026/2027 school year.
• >46,500 children had their education interrupted due to the closure of learning spaces in 2026.
• ~93% of school buildings (526 out of 564) will require full reconstruction or major
rehabilitation to be functional again, as of 11 October 2025.
• >63 university buildings destroyed (source: MoE, 12 August 2025).
*Source: Education Cluster Situation and Advocacy Paper, as of September 2026, unless otherwise noted.

HEALTH SERVICES FUNCTIONALITY** (as of 30 September 2026)

HEALTH*

• 30 Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) including 104 national and 75
international personnel, as of 30 September 2026.
• Between 23 and 29 September, 156 patients, including 64 children, and 183
companions were evacuated via Rafah and Kerem Shalom crossings.
• Since the ceaseﬁre agreement was announced on 10 October 2025, 3,385
patients and 5,646 companions were evacuated via Rafah and Kerem Shalom
crossings, with support from WHO. Of these, 2,610 patients and 3,886
companions were evacuated via Rafah since it reopened on 2 February 2026
(as of 29 September 2026).
• Over 43,000 of the people injured since October 2023 are estimated to have
potentially life-changing injuries. (source: WHO, as of May 2026).

EGYPT

**** The reported Israeli casualties are soldiers killed or injured since the
start of the ground operation (source: Israeli military website).

• >1.4 million (67% of the population) are expected to face Crisis or worse levels of acute food
insecurity in July-December 2026, up from 1.2 million people (59%) between mid-April and
30 June 2026. (source: IPC, 23 July 2026).
• ~1.9 million (90% of the pop.) would face high levels of acute food insecurity through
December 2026 in the absence of humanitarian food assistance. (source: IPC, 23 July 2026).
• 2 meals a day on average were consumed by most surveyed households.
• 3% of surveyed households went a full day without eating at least once in the last 30 days.
• 21% of surveyed households consumed only one meal a day.
• 56% of surveyed households in Gaza and North Gaza governorates, and 59% of surveyed
households in Deir al Balah and Khan Younis governorates relied on humanitarian aid as
their primary source of food.
• 78% of surveyed households relied on waste burning to prepare food.
• 16.6% of greenhouse area is undamaged and accessible (source: FAO and UNOSAT, as of
24 June 2026).
• 3% of Gaza’s cropland is undamaged and accessible (source: FAO and UNOSAT, as of 24
June 2026).
*Source: WFP Gaza Market Monitor, Mid-August 2026, unless otherwise specified.

REPORTED DAMAGE*

92% of assessed establishments in the commerce and industry sector are destroyed or damaged.
74% of the road network is destroyed and 13% is damaged.
88% of above-ground WASH assets and 76% of underground networks are damaged.
83% of the Gaza Strip’s coastal zone is fully or partially destroyed
76% of assessed cultural and heritage sites are destroyed or damaged.
90% of energy infrastructure including electricity distribution network and associated assets are
destroyed.
• 82% of all structures are destroyed or damaged (source: UNOSAT, as of 16 June 2026).
*Source: Gaza Strip RDNA as of October 2025, issued in April 2026, unless otherwise specified.

SHELTER*

• 1.98 million people (94% of the population) estimated to need shelter and NFI assistance,
including about 1.2 million people (58%) facing Critical (Phase 4) or Catastrophic (Phase 5) shelter
conditions.
• 65% of assessed households were living in tents or makeshift shelters, of which 54% were in poor
or very poor condition.
• 76.6% of housing units (371,888 out of 485,361) destroyed or damaged (source: UN, EU and the
World Bank, Gaza Strip RDNA as of October 2025, issued in April 2026).
• >950,000 people are estimated to live in 989 displacement sites at medium or high ﬂood risk,
including over 400,000 people in 451 high-risk sites (source: Shelter Cluster, Site Management
Cluster and IOM Gaza Flooding Risk Assessment as of September 2026).
*Source: Shelter severity and household needs assessment, August 2026 (data collected in June 2026), unless otherwise specified.

Facilitated: CLA accepts a facilitation request and the movement on the ground is not impeded.
Impeded: CLA accepts a facilitation request but the movement is blocked or delayed
on the ground, resulting in some missions being aborted or accomplished partially.
Denied: The Israeli Coordination and Liaison Administration (CLA) rejects a facilitation request.
Withdrawn: Humanitarian organizations cancel their facilitation request due to
logistical, operational, or security reasons.
